column1: # census-verdicts.tsv — FROZEN VERDICTS: what the branch↔roadmap matcher answers for each
# of the 205 governed branches this repository ever had, against census-roadmaps.txt.
#   gh pr list --state all --limit 600 --json headRefName   (feat/ fix/ refactor/ only)
# = 205 distinct branch names. Frozen for the same reason as the roadmap list: neither `gh`
# nor the reflog is reachable from a CI checkout, and a corpus the CI cannot reach is a
#   verdict = accept | block   — `accept` means `trackfw branch new --dry-run <branch>`
#             substring = accepted by the HISTORICAL arm (strings.Contains), i.e. it already
#             tokens    = accepted ONLY by the new token-overlap arm — these 14 are exactly
#                         the branches ML-3A's change repaired. Measured by rebuilding with
#             none      = rejected by both arms. 15 branches.
# 🔴 THE 15 `block` ROWS ARE NOT A BUG — DO NOT "FIX" THEM BY LOWERING THE THRESHOLD.
# strings.Contains rejected 29 of the 205 (14%, ML-3A census). The token arm closes 14 of
# them; these 15 are the measured residual. They are pre-governance branches whose title
# shares fewer than 2 content tokens of 3+ chars with any roadmap in the corpus (e.g.
# feat/agents-command against ROADMAP-…-agent-rules-inject-…). At N=1 ALL 205 are accepted —
# the relation stops discriminating entirely — which is exactly the floor that forced N=2.
# Widening the threshold to accept these 15 destroys the rule, it does not fix the corpus.
# Arithmetic that ties these numbers to the ML-3A audit, independent of this file:
# Both identities are re-derived by the gate's self-test from a substring-only build.
